text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- An additional old-age pension rise will take place as of July 1, 1997, following parliamentary approval.
The rise will be based on consumer price growth reported in the fourth quarter of 1995, Labour Minister Andrzej Baczkowski said.
- Fiat's car plants in Tychy and Bielsko Biala in southern Poland will make 300,000 cars this year, showing slight growth compared with last year's results.
In 1995 Fiat Auto Poland exported 50 percent of its total production.
- By November 19 Mostostal Zabrze construction firm will produce its project for the Opel car plant it wants to build for General Motors in Gliwice, southern Poland, where GM has chosen a site.
- Around 59 percent of Poland's households have economised on meat purchases in 1996 due to growing meat prices, a survey by the PBS polling institute said.
- Polish companies invested more than 20.5 billion zlotys in the first eight months of 1996, mostly in production development.
Investments grew faster in the private sector and made up almost half of total investment, the Central Statistical Office said.
- Pork and beef prices went down by 0.06 zloty and 0.01 zloty respectively last week.

No further price decrease will follow and slight price growth may be expected before the coming All Saints Day and Independance Day holidays, Pekpol meat and fodder exchange president Wlodzimierz Gadomski said.
NOWA EUROPA
- A European Institute will be set up in Lodz, central Poland, to train Polish civil service members for the needs of European integration.

- Centrist opposition Union for Freedom (UW) Chairman Leszek Balcerowicz has accused the ruling coalition of the ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) and Polish Peasants Party (PSL) of delaying and giving up on some of the country's economic reforms.
- The number of work-related injuries rose by 4.3 percent in the first six months of 1996 compared with the same period last year, the Central Statistical Office said.
The biggest number of injuries -- 30,000 -- was reported in state-owned companies.
- The president of the Warsaw-based Daewoo-FSO car plant Soek Jin Chul and other high ranking Daewoo executives were arrested on Saturday in Korea's expanding corruption scandal.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- The Era GSM digital mobile phone network has increased its span by linking subscribers in the cities of Gliwice, Lodz and Tychy, and will soon add subscribers in Wroclaw and Szczecin. Era's main competitor, Plus GSM, currently boasts 3,500 subscribers with 300 new subscribers joining daily.
- The number of Polish farms has decreased by 130,000 in the last eight years, an agricultural sector census conducted this year showed.
ZYCIE WARSZAWY
- An improvement in officers' living standards is not accompanying the reform of the Polish army, Polish officers complain.

- Poland's Catholic church and the government ignore minority churches, and the constitutional right of equality of denominations is abused, representatives of Polish protestants, buddhists, moslems and other religions said.
